div.head: IV Eg 15
div.ab: Þonne fyrþrige Oslác eorl ⁊ éal here, þe on his ealdor[do]me wunað, þæt þis stande, Gode to lofe ⁊ ure ealra saula to þearfe ⁊ eallum folce to friðe.
Þonne fyrðrige Oslác eorl ⁊ eall here, þe on ðis ealdordome wunað, þæt ðis stande, Gode to lofe ⁊ ure ealra saula to ðearfe ⁊ eallum folce to friðe.

ad pacis abundantiam Deoque, omnium saluatori, ad laudem et magnificentiam et nobis omnibus in hac terrena peregrinatione degentibus ad uite longinquitatem nostrorumque peccaminum abolitionem et remissionem.
Þonne fyrðrige Oslác eorl ⁊ eall here þe on his ealdordome wunað, þæt ðis stande, Gode to lofe ⁊ ure ealra saula to ðearfe ⁊ eallum folce to friðe.

Further, Earl Oslac and all the population dwelling in his earldom shall promote the observance of this, to the praise of God, and for the good of the souls of all of us, and the security of the whole nation.

Now Earl Oslac and all the host who dwell in his aldormanry are to give their support that this may be enforced, for the praise of God and the benefit of the souls of all of us and the security of all people.

Nun befördere Earl Oslac und das ganze ‘Heer’ [der Nordleute], das in seinem [Northumbrischen] Herzogthume wohnt, dass Obiges gelte, Gott zum Lobe und zum Nutzen unser aller Seelen und allem Volke zur Sicherheit.

Now let Earl Oslac and the whole ‘army’ [of the Northmen] which lives in his [Northumbrian] ealdormanry promote that the above stand, to the praise of God and the benefit of all our souls and the security of all the people.
div.note: F's ‘ealdor[do]me’ is corrected in other ink from ‘ealdorme’.
id. omits this chapter, and so has no reference to Earl Oslac of Northumbria.
The word here, originally meaning a raiding army, came to be used of the inhabitants of the Danish settlements, without any military significance.
